newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - Dec 18.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- New head of Ivory Coast's Caisse de Stabilisation cocoa and coffee marketing board, Yves-Marie Koissy, says after meeting President Henri Konan Bedie he plans to launch liberalisation and restructing at the start of 1997 but declines to go into detail

- Two-day taxi strike in commercial capital Abidjan ends after talks with Security Minister Marcel Dibonan Kone about plan for police to detain, for the purposes of investigation, all taxi drivers who say they have been heldup by bandits; Dibonan says drivers should not be held for more than a day.
- Donors, government officials and representatives of small businesses hold seminar to discuss ways of expanding the sector.
- Ivorian company Africa Bell and France Telecom top bidders for 51 percent stake in privatised Ivorian state telecommunications company CI-TELCOM; privatisation committee examines bids in detail

- African Development Bank aims to crack down on arrears, review its lending rate and improve management of its foreign exchange holdings and revenue, its president Omar Kabbaj tells ambassadors in Ivory Coast; bank will seek to attack poverty by targeting private sector growth, job creation and economic integration.
- French cotton company CFDT, traditional marketing heavyweight in Francophone West Africa, says privatisation in the sector carries risks for peasant farmers
